THE EDITORIAL STANDARD

Trust comes from showing the work.

DocAtlas helps engineers make a smaller, better-informed shortlist. Public evidence and visible limitations are the starting point.

What belongs here

Tools that directly support document parsing, extraction, structured records, semantic modeling, retrieval, or grounded answers. Semantic foundations may take metadata and structured data rather than raw files.

General chat interfaces, annotation-only platforms, and broad office suites fall outside this directory.

How profiles are built

  1. Check the official project or product source.
  2. Identify the task, inputs, outputs, and runtime dependencies.
  3. Separate confirmed documentation from claims that need sample validation.
  4. Record limitations and link readers back to the original source.

What a Featured Tool means

A pick is useful for a named workflow and has enough public detail to evaluate. We consider task fit, technical documentation, outputs and attribution, deployment, licensing, and inspectable limitations. It is not a claim that the tool beats all alternatives.

Evidence levels

Source review: a summary of official documentation. Current profiles and picks use this level. Hands-on evaluation: reserved for future work with published samples, versions, methods, and results. We do not label a source review as a test.

Commercial relationships

Editorial placement is not for sale. This edition contains no paid placements or affiliate links. Any future sponsorship or affiliate relationship must be disclosed beside the affected link or placement.

How to read capabilities

Code availability, model weights, and commercial rights are separate questions. Page citations, bounding boxes, semantic evidence, and database lineage are different forms of provenance.

Corrections and updates

Source-review dates describe documentation checks, not a promise of continuous monitoring. If a capability or link has changed, email a correction through the submission page. Suggestions remain unpublished until editorial review.
